items.followUp: Write the electronic configuration of Mg²⁺ and state the number of electrons in its outermost shell.

rubric.why: The ion has 10 electrons after losing three electrons from a neutral aluminium atom.
rubric.how: Award for the shell configuration or the equivalent subshell configuration containing 10 electrons.

rubric.why: The second shell is the outermost occupied shell and contains eight electrons.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the outermost shell contains 8 electrons.

modelAnswer: Al has 13 electrons; Al³⁺ has lost 3 electrons and has 10 electrons.

items.followUp: Explain why atomic radius generally decreases across a period.

rubric.why: Electron affinity generally becomes greater from left to right across a period.
rubric.description: Correct periodic trend in electron affinity.
rubric.how: Award for stating that electron affinity increases across a period.

rubric.why: Increasing nuclear charge with little additional shielding strengthens the attraction for an added electron.
rubric.description: Reason for the increase in electron affinity.
rubric.how: Award for linking the trend to stronger nuclear attraction for the added electron.

modelAnswer: Electron affinity generally increases from left to right across a period.
The nuclear charge increases, so the atom attracts an added electron more strongly.

items.followUp: State the trend in atomic radius across a period and down a group.

rubric.why: Ionization energy generally rises across a period.
rubric.how: Award for stating that ionization energy increases from left to right across a period.

rubric.why: Ionization energy generally falls down a group.
rubric.how: Award for stating that ionization energy decreases down a group.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy generally increases from left to right across a period.
Ionization energy generally decreases down a group.

items.followUp: How many elements are in the second period of the periodic table? Name them.

rubric.why: The first period contains only two elements.
rubric.how: Award for stating that there are 2 elements.

rubric.why: Hydrogen and helium are the two elements in the first period.
rubric.how: Award for naming both hydrogen and helium.

modelAnswer: The first period contains 2 elements: hydrogen and helium.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a cation and an anion.

rubric.why: The octet rule describes stability associated with eight electrons in the outermost shell.
rubric.how: Award for stating that an atom tends to attain eight outermost-shell electrons.

rubric.why: The duplet rule describes stability associated with two electrons in the first shell.
rubric.how: Award for stating that an atom tends to attain two electrons in its first shell.

modelAnswer: According to the octet rule, atoms tend to gain, lose or share electrons to attain 8 electrons in their outermost shell.
According to the duplet rule, atoms tend to attain 2 electrons in their first shell.

items.followUp: Explain how sodium and chlorine form an ionic bond.

rubric.why: A Group 1 atom loses one electron and a Group 17 atom gains one electron to attain stable outer shells.
rubric.description: Electron transfer between Group 1 and Group 17 elements.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the loss of one electron by Group 1 and its gain by Group 17.

rubric.why: The resulting oppositely charged ions attract one another.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions as an ionic bond.

modelAnswer: A Group 1 atom loses one electron, while a Group 17 atom gains that electron; both attain stable outer shells.
The oppositely charged ions attract each other by electrostatic force and form an ionic bond.

items.followUp: Define boiling and freezing, and state how each differs from the other.

rubric.why: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the change from liquid to vapour.

rubric.why: Condensation is the change of vapour into liquid.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the change from vapour to liquid.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface.
Condensation is the change of vapour into liquid, usually on cooling.

items.followUp: Calculate the percentage mass of a solution containing 12 g of solute in 88 g of solvent.

rubric.why: The mass percentage compares the mass of solute with the total mass of solution.
rubric.description: Correct mass ratio in the definition.
rubric.how: Award for giving mass of solute divided by mass of solution.

rubric.why: Multiplying the ratio by 100 expresses it as a percentage.
rubric.description: Conversion of the ratio to a percentage.
rubric.how: Award for multiplying the mass ratio by 100.

modelAnswer: Percentage mass (% m/m) is the mass of solute divided by the mass of solution, multiplied by 100.
% m/m = (mass of solute ÷ mass of solution) × 100.
